AgentCompass v0.7.3 makes a model you name reach the bundle you named, and stops the background Antigravity usage read from opening browser sign-in pages.

- **A bare name means any account.** `gpt-5.5` names that model's bundles on every account, whatever prefix an account lists it under. One account being unchecked, exhausted or unavailable never blocks another.
- **A prefix is obeyed.** `openai/gpt-5.5` names only the bundles that prefix names: a bundle listed under exactly that spelling, or that model on the account, provider, serving provider or Magpie preset with that id. When those cannot run, the answer says so and lists each with its reason; the same model on another account is not substituted. This changes v0.7.2, where a prefixed name could also launch another account's bare bundle: write the bare name when any account will do.
- **A prefix that names nothing on your fleet is ignored.** If no account, provider or listing carries the prefix, the rest is read as the name: `openai/gpt-5.5` on a fleet where nobody is `openai` is `gpt-5.5`. This also holds for a provider you do not have: `opencode/deepseek-v4-flash` without an OpenCode account is read as `deepseek-v4-flash`.
- **Fixed after v0.7.2.** Naming `opencode/deepseek-v4-flash` (OpenCode lists other weights under that name) could launch `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` on the account beside it, and `record` rewrote the named model onto the other row. A named model is now matched among every bundle that exists on the addressed accounts before any filter of preference, availability or effort, with one rule read by `plan`, `record`, `prepare`, `roll --resume`, temporary priorities, the spawn gate and the tray's quick targets.
- **Malformed names are refused.** `/gpt-5.5` and `openai/` get a message instead of being read as the bare name. A temporary priority already stored with such a name is kept, matches nothing and expires on its own.
- **`-preview` names.** A name that differs from a row only by `-preview` is that row on every provider.
- **Magpie presets.** A Magpie preset whose id differs from the models.dev catalog it serves (17 presets, for example `opencode-zen` and `tencent-cloud`) is read as that catalog, on Magpie accounts only. The data schema stays 8; v0.7.1 and v0.7.2 accept the published set.
- **No more sign-in pages from the usage read.** On one machine the token refresh failed on a network error for some hours while the sign-in itself was intact; each background `agy -p /usage` then started an interactive sign-in and opened the browser, twice per five-minute pass. The read now runs in a job of one process, which refuses the program agy starts to open the page, and a read that reached its time limit is not run again. The Usage Float plugin has the same change.

Not verified: agy's interactive sign-in under the one-process limit was not reproduced end to end (its silent sign-in could not be made to fail without touching the stored sign-in); the evidence is that the limit refuses every program agy starts while the usage read still answers. The scorer's agy call is a model turn that needs helper processes and is not limited, so it can still open one page per dispatch when agy is the scorer in use and its token refresh fails. A live launch of a prefixed name through a gateway account was not run. The local Windows Sandbox installer check was not run for this release.

The Windows tray installer is unsigned; Windows SmartScreen may warn on first launch. See [packaging/SIGNING.md](https://github.com/akiiwa-games/AgentCompass/blob/v0.7.3/packaging/SIGNING.md).

Status: alpha. Accounts come from discovery on your machine; choose which ones take part in the tray.
